pointers.sentence: The bound field keeps the form, the field and its name, settles its names and label when it is made, keeps the initial value and the widget's parts once worked out, and works out the data, the value and the errors each time it is asked (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField`).

`BaseForm.__getitem__` makes a name's bound field the first time it is asked for, by `Field.get_bound_field`, and keeps it: a form has one for each name (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__getitem__`).
The class is the field's `bound_field_class`, else the form's, else `BoundField` (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.get_bound_field`).
The form's was settled in `BaseForm.__init__`: its argument, else its class's, else the renderer's `BaseRenderer.bound_field_class` (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).
`BoundField.__init__` settles the field's names in the HTML (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.__init__`).
The label is the field's, or else the name made readable by `pretty_name`: underscores become spaces, the first letter a capital and the rest lower case (`django/forms/utils.py:pretty_name`).

`BoundField.auto_id` comes from the form's `auto_id`: a string with `%s` in it is filled with the html name, another true value is the html name itself, and a false one gives `""`, and so no `"aria-describedby"` and, unless the widget has an id of its own, no `"id"` and no label element (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.auto_id`).
`BoundField.id_for_label`, the id a label points at, is the widget's own `"id"` or else `auto_id`, as `Widget.id_for_label` gives it back (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.id_for_label`).
A `MultiWidget` and a `RadioSelect` give back `""`, so their label points at no input (`django/forms/widgets.py:MultiWidget.id_for_label`).

For radio buttons the docstring says this improves accessibility when using a screen reader, and that clicking such a label would toggle the first input (`django/forms/widgets.py:RadioSelect.id_for_label`).

`BoundField.data` is what was submitted: the field's widget reads it out of the form's data and files under the html name at each use; the base widget gives `None` when nothing is there (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm._widget_data_value`).
It is a cached property, so a callable initial is called once in a form's life (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.initial`).
`BoundField.value` is what the input shows (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.value`).
A bound one shows what `Field.bound_data` makes of the data and the initial: in the base class the data, but the initial for a disabled field (`django/forms/fields.py:Field.bound_data`).

`BaseForm.changed_data` asks each bound field `BoundField._has_changed`, which hands `Field.has_changed` an initial value and `data` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField._has_changed`, `django/forms/fields.py:Field.has_changed`).

`BaseForm.changed_data` asks each bound field `BoundField._has_changed`, which hands `Field.has_changed` an initial value and `data` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField._has_changed`, `django/forms/fields.py:Field.has_changed`).

Such a field is drawn with a hidden input after its widget, by `as_hidden(only_initial=True)`, named `html_initial_name`, with the id `html_initial_id`, and holding `value`, or on a redraw what was submitted under that name (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableFieldMixin.__str__`, `django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).

Such a field is drawn with a hidden input after its widget, by `as_hidden(only_initial=True)`, named `html_initial_name`, with the id `html_initial_id`, and holding `value`, or on a redraw what was submitted under that name (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableFieldMixin.__str__`, `django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).

`str(form["tonnage"])`, what `{{ form.tonnage }}` prints, is the widget alone: `RenderableFieldMixin` replaces the `__str__` and `__html__` of `RenderableMixin` with `as_widget`, and the hidden initial input when the field asks for one (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableFieldMixin`).

It marks the widget localized if the field is, adds attributes by `build_widget_attrs`, gives `auto_id` as the `"id"` unless the widget or the attributes passed have one, and has it render the html name and `value` with the form's renderer (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).
`BoundField.build_widget_attrs` copies the attributes it is given and adds these (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`):
The widget has a say in `"required"` (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget.use_required_attribute`).
`BoundField.errors` is the form's list for the name, or an empty one of the form's `error_class` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.errors`).
It is empty for a hidden field or one with no id, and `None` when the widget has an `"aria-describedby"` of its own (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.aria_describedby`).
`BoundField.label_tag` draws the label (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.label_tag`).

`BoundField.css_classes` gives the classes for the element around a field: those passed, with the form's `"error_css_class"` if the field has errors and its `"required_css_class"` if it is required (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.css_classes`).

`BoundField.subwidgets` asks the field's widget for its parts, with the html name, `value` and the attributes `build_widget_attrs` makes, and wraps each in a `BoundWidget` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.subwidgets`).
The base widget has one part; a choice widget has one for each option (`django/forms/widgets.py:ChoiceWidget.subwidgets`).

A `BoundWidget` renders its part with `BoundWidget.tag`, and as a string with `"wrap_label"` set, which puts a radio button inside its label; `BoundWidget.choice_label` and `BoundWidget.id_for_label` read the option's label and id (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundWidget`).

`BoundField.__getitem__` takes only an integer or a slice, and raises `TypeError` for anything else before it touches the list, to prevent, its comment says, needless re-evaluation when a template reads its attributes (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.__getitem__`).
`BoundField.widget_type` is the widget's class name in lower case, less a final `"widget"` or `"input"`: `"number"` for a `NumberInput` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.widget_type`).
